docs.text:
The fundamental theorem of calculus states that if \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(F(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\, dt\), then

\[ F'(x) = f(x). \]

docs.title: Algebra
docs.text: Notes on abstract algebra: groups, rings, fields, and their homomorphisms.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Group Theory — definitions, Lagrange's theorem, homomorphisms.
  • Ring Theory — ideals, quotients, polynomial rings.

docs.title: Notation
docs.text: Symbol Meaning \(G, H\) Groups \(R\) A ring \(\leq\) Subgroup \(\trianglelefteq\) Normal subgroup \(\cong\) Isomorphic

docs.title: 1. Definition of a Group
docs.text:
A group is a pair \((G, \cdot)\) where \(G\) is a set and \(\cdot : G \times G \to G\) is a binary operation satisfying:

  1. Associativity: \((ab)c = a(bc)\) for all \(a,b,c \in G\).
  2. Identity: there exists \(e \in G\) such that \(eg = ge = g\) for all \(g \in G\).
  3. Inverses: for each \(g \in G\), there exists \(g^{-1} \in G\) with \(gg^{-1} = g^{-1}g = e\).

If additionally \(ab = ba\) for all \(a, b \in G\), the group is called abelian.

docs.title: 2. Subgroups
docs.text:
A subset \(H \subseteq G\) is a subgroup, written \(H \leq G\), if \(H\) is itself a group under the restriction of \(\cdot\).

Subgroup Criterion

A nonempty \(H \subseteq G\) is a subgroup iff for all \(a, b \in H\), we have \(ab^{-1} \in H\).

docs.title: 3. Lagrange's Theorem
docs.text:
If \(G\) is a finite group and \(H \leq G\), then \(|H|\) divides \(|G|\), and in fact

\[ |G| = [G : H] \cdot |H|. \]

Consider the left cosets \(gH = \{gh : h \in H\}\). They partition \(G\), and each has cardinality \(|H|\) via the bijection \(h \mapsto gh\). Hence \(|G| = k \cdot |H|\) where \(k = [G : H]\) is the number of distinct cosets.

docs.title: Corollaries
docs.text:
1. The order of any element \(g \in G\) divides \(|G|\).
  2. If \(|G| = p\) is prime, then \(G \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\).

docs.title: 4. Homomorphisms
docs.text:
A map \(\varphi : G \to H\) is a homomorphism if \(\varphi(ab) = \varphi(a)\varphi(b)\) for all \(a, b \in G\).

  • \(\ker \varphi = \{g \in G : \varphi(g) = e_H\}\) is a normal subgroup.
  • \(\operatorname{im} \varphi \leq H\).
  • First isomorphism theorem: \(G / \ker \varphi \cong \operatorname{im} \varphi\).

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Show that \((\mathbb{Z}, +)\) is a group, but \((\mathbb{Z}, \cdot)\) is not.
  2. Prove that every group of order \(4\) is abelian.
  3. Classify all groups of order \(6\).

docs.title: 1. Definition
docs.text:
A ring is a triple \((R, +, \cdot)\) such that:

  • \((R, +)\) is an abelian group.
  • Multiplication is associative: \((ab)c = a(bc)\).
  • Distributivity holds: \(a(b+c) = ab + ac\) and \((a+b)c = ac + bc\).

If \(R\) also has a multiplicative identity \(1\), we call \(R\) a unital ring. If \(ab = ba\) for all \(a,b\), \(R\) is commutative.

docs.title: 2. Ideals
docs.text:
A subset \(I \subseteq R\) is an ideal if:

  1. \((I, +)\) is a subgroup of \((R, +)\).
  2. For all \(r \in R\) and \(x \in I\): \(rx \in I\) and \(xr \in I\).

The quotient \(R / I\) inherits a ring structure.

First Isomorphism Theorem for Rings. If \(\varphi : R \to S\) is a ring homomorphism, then

\[ R / \ker \varphi \cong \operatorname{im} \varphi. \]

docs.title: 3. Polynomial Rings
docs.text: For a commutative ring \(R\), \(R[x]\) is the ring of polynomials with coefficients in \(R\). If \(R\) is a field, \(R[x]\) is a Euclidean domain.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Show that \(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\) is a field iff \(n\) is prime.
  2. Prove that every ideal of \(\mathbb{Z}\) is principal.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text: Notes on real analysis and calculus.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Limits — \(\varepsilon\)-\(\delta\) definitions and properties.
  • Integration — Riemann integrals, FTC, and techniques.

docs.title: Core Definitions
docs.text:
• Limit: \(\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L\) iff for every \(\varepsilon > 0\) there exists \(\delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - a| < \delta \Rightarrow |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon\).
  • Continuity: \(f\) is continuous at \(a\) iff \(\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)\).

docs.title: 1. The Riemann Integral
docs.text:
Given \(f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}\) bounded, a partition \(P = \{x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n\}\) of \([a,b]\) has mesh \(\|P\| = \max_i (x_i - x_{i-1})\).

Upper and lower sums:

\[ U(f, P) = \sum_{i=1}^n M_i \Delta x_i, \qquad L(f, P) = \sum_{i=1}^n m_i \Delta x_i \]

where \(M_i = \sup_{[x_{i-1}, x_i]} f\) and \(m_i = \inf_{[x_{i-1}, x_i]} f\).

\(f\) is Riemann integrable if \(\sup_P L(f, P) = \inf_P U(f, P)\); call this common value \(\int_a^b f\).

docs.title: 2. Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
docs.text:
FTC, Part I. If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and \(F(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\, dt\), then \(F\) is differentiable on \((a,b)\) and

\[ F'(x) = f(x). \]

FTC, Part II. If \(f\) is integrable and \(F\) is any antiderivative of \(f\), then

\[ \int_a^b f(x)\, dx = F(b) - F(a). \]

docs.title: 3. Techniques
docs.text: Technique When to use Substitution Composite integrands Integration by parts Products, \(\int u \, dv = uv - \int v \, du\) Partial fractions Rational functions Trigonometric substitution \(\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\), etc.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Compute \(\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx\) directly from the definition.
  2. Evaluate \(\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x \, dx\) using \(\sin^2 x = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\).

docs.title: 1. The \(\varepsilon\)-\(\delta\) Definition
docs.text:
Let \(f : D \to \mathbb{R}\) and let \(a\) be a limit point of \(D\). We say

\[ \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L \]

if for every \(\varepsilon > 0\), there exists \(\delta > 0\) such that

\[ 0 < |x - a| < \delta \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon. \]

docs.title: 2. Basic Limit Laws
docs.text:
If \(\lim_{x\to a} f(x) = L\) and \(\lim_{x\to a} g(x) = M\), then:

  • \(\lim_{x \to a} (f + g)(x) = L + M\)
  • \(\lim_{x \to a} (fg)(x) = LM\)
  • If \(M \neq 0\), \(\lim_{x \to a} (f/g)(x) = L/M\)

docs.title: 3. An Important Limit
docs.text:
\[ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} = 1. \]

For \(0 < x < \pi/2\), consider the unit circle. Comparing areas of the inscribed triangle, the sector, and the outer triangle gives

\[ \sin x < x < \tan x. \]

Dividing by \(\sin x\) and taking reciprocals:

\[ \cos x < \frac{\sin x}{x} < 1. \]

By the squeeze theorem and \(\cos x \to 1\) as \(x \to 0\), the result follows.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Prove that \(\lim_{x \to 2} (3x + 1) = 7\) from the definition.
  2. Show that \(\lim_{x \to 0} x^2 \sin(1/x) = 0\).
